learning_outcomes.text: Have profound knowledge of conventional technologies in manufacturing processes.
Know and understand arguments of metallic materials manufacturing and machining.
Understand and explain the meaning of conventional manufacturing processes applied to traditional materials.
Understand the fundamental concepts concerning the choice of the best technology to manufacture a product and be aware of potential applications in other fields.
Demonstrate skilled reasoning in traditional manufacturing processes and the ability to conceive principles of conventional machining of products.
Be able to read and understand other texts on related topics.

syllabus_topics: Properties of materials relevant to different technological processes

Fundamentals of Metal Casting: cast structures of solidified metals, basic types of cast structures, segregation, shrinkage of casting, shrinkage stresses, common casting defects, general design rules for casting, materials and processes classification
Welding technology: analysis and classification of the essential processes
Forging of metals: characteristics of forging, cold and hot plastic deformation
Extrusion of metals: direct-extrusion, products made from extrusions, types of extrusion, process variables in extrusion, extrusion force, impact extrusion
Fundamentals of machining: tool geometry, cutting process analysis, tool wear, tool materials, surface integrity of workpiece
Machining processes used to produce various shapes: milling, drilling, broaching, abrasive machining and finishing operations
Non-destructive testing (visual inspection, radiography, gamma-ray, ultrasonic testing, penetrating liquids, magnetoscopy, eddy current testing, thermography, and acoustic emission)
teaching_methods: Interaction with students through problem proposition and decision-making
Participation in guided exercises (classroom and laboratory)

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam on plastic deformation processes
Oral exam on machining by chip removal

assessment_rules: The final exam consists of answering several questions on manufacturing processes in approximately an hour. Passing requires demonstration of minimum knowledge and skills in essential characteristics of the foundry process, identification of main plastic deformation processes, identification of main machining operations by chip removal, and essential characteristics of the welding process. Grades reflect four levels of preparation: sufficient, adequate, good, and very good. There are no formal prerequisite verifications, but the teacher highlights essential knowledge at the first lesson.
